samples.prompt: Some people support the proposal that teachers should allow phones for carefully planned classroom activities. Others believe practical difficulties should be addressed before it is introduced widely. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

samples.summaryVi: Điện thoại có ích khi có nhiệm vụ rõ; thông báo và luật dùng không rõ dễ gây xao nhãng.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: There are different views about the proposal that teachers should allow phones for carefully planned classroom activities. Supporters emphasise its usefulness, while others believe that practical difficulties should be dealt with before it is introduced more widely. Both positions have reasonable concerns. In my opinion, the idea is worth supporting when those difficulties are addressed.
paragraphs.noteVi: Giới thiệu hai phía và ý kiến cá nhân.

parts.labelVi: Nêu quan điểm cá nhân

parts.text: the idea is worth supporting when those difficulties are addressed.

paragraphs.label: Quan điểm thứ nhất
paragraphs.text: On the one hand, supporters focus on the benefits. One important point in favour of the proposal is that students can quickly access useful learning material. This is possible because a shared task can direct phone use towards a specific question rather than casual browsing. For example, a class can compare two digital maps to explain how a neighbourhood has changed. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.label: Quan điểm thứ hai
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, a more cautious view deserves attention. A difficulty that should not be ignored is that notifications can distract students. This matters because a device used for learning also gives access to games and private messages. For instance, a pupil may stop following a discussion after receiving several messages from friends. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

paragraphs.text: My own view is that the potential benefit is worth pursuing, but the conditions matter. In particular, it would be sensible to agree on specific times for phone use and keep devices away during other tasks. People should be able to understand what is expected and raise difficulties before those difficulties become a reason to give up. A flexible plan is therefore more convincing than a promise that the same method will work equally well for everyone.

paragraphs.label: Quan điểm thứ hai
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, a more cautious view deserves attention. A difficulty that should not be ignored is that an unrealistic rule may lead to arguments rather than better habits. This matters because parents and children may disagree about when an online match can reasonably be stopped. For instance, a parent may demand an immediate stop in the middle of a team game that was arranged in advance. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

paragraphs.label: Ý kiến của tôi
paragraphs.text: My own view is that the potential benefit is worth pursuing, but the conditions matter. In particular, it would be sensible to agree on realistic finishing times and responsibilities before play begins. People should be able to understand what is expected and raise difficulties before those difficulties become a reason to give up. A flexible plan is therefore more convincing than a promise that the same method will work equally well for everyone.

paragraphs.label: Kết bài
paragraphs.text: In conclusion, one side is right to recognise the potential value, while the other is right to ask how the idea will work in practice. I support a planned and flexible approach that pursues the benefit without overlooking the people who may face difficulties.
